prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The baseline fell into the trivial policy of choosing DONE at step 1 (0 reward), so it never learned to build anything. The untrained trace shows why. Every placement landed mirrored in x: the cells filled were at actual x = X − dx − x_action, while rows were unchanged (1x1 at col 2 filled col 5; 1x2 at col 6 filled cols 0–1; 2x2 at col 6 filled cols 0–1). The observation itself is not mirrored. So the convolutional head scores each action from the features of the wrong, mirrored cells. A local, shift-equivariant net cannot easily learn that remapping, so every placement it tries is penalised and DONE wins. Flipping the feature map in x before the footprint-pooling head fixes this exactly. Pooling the flipped map over the action's window covers precisely the cells the brick will fill. This round tests that fix with the default recipe, with a recipe tweak, and in a version that does not assume the mirror.

### Round 2
Placement in this world is mirrored in x: action column x fills columns X-dx-x to X-1-x. Flipping the trunk features in x before the footprint-pooling head fixes this and lifts dev success from 0 to 0.75 (r1c1). Two training changes on top raised it to 0.89 (r1c2): more updates (128 envs, 3 epochs, 1.3x the samples) and gamma 0.98. That gap of 15 points is well above the per-seed spread of about 3–6 points. r1c3 fed the head both orientations and a deeper trunk and dropped to 0.47. It had fewer samples and learned more slowly, so a known hard prior beats learning the mapping. We seem to be short of samples: r1c2's training success levels off near 0.84, dev IoU is 0.98, and it places about 0.47 wrong cells per episode, so the misses are small mistakes. Trials take about 76 s against a 900 s limit. The next levers are fewer PPO epochs, which buys more fresh samples, and cheap changes that make it easier for the head to match each footprint's landing layer against the target.

### Round 3
Flipping the head in x is what made the agent work (0 → 0.75–0.89). Fewer PPO epochs gives more samples, and the good seeds improved: 0.912 with 2 epochs and 0.953 with 1 epoch, against 0.89 for r1c2's 3 epochs. With 1 epoch, training success reached 0.90 and dev IoU 0.993. But seed 1 scored 0.0 under both 1 and 2 epochs, so the 2-seed means fell to about 0.46. That looks like a collapse that depends on the seed. The likely cause, which I have not confirmed, is the early DONE trap seen in the starting architecture: random placements earn negative reward and DONE earns 0. The stem skip (r2c2) and the 3-conv hedge (r1c3) were worse, so the architecture is not the bottleneck. The 1-epoch recipe has the highest score when it works. This round tests ways to stop the collapse: a higher entropy bonus at 1 and at 2 epochs, and a lower learning rate. Each change is checked across both seeds.

### Round 4
Flipping the head's x-axis is the key fix: placement actions are mirrored in x. Every unflipped network collapsed to choosing DONE at once. Beyond that, the main risk is collapse caused by seed luck. Placements are penalised early in training while DONE scores 0. So 1 epoch (r2c3, r3c1, r3c3) and 2 epochs at entropy 0.01 (r2c1) each lost at least one seed to DONE. Lowering lr made collapse certain. With 2 epochs and entropy 0.03 (r3c2), both seeds survived, giving the best score, 0.936 (0.926/0.945). 3 epochs at entropy 0.01 (r1c2, 0.89) was stable but had fewer samples. The architecture changes so far (both orientations plus depth; stem skip into the head) did worse, partly through slower learning. Dev IoU is about 0.99, so the remaining errors are small. For this final round I make single changes to r3c2: a stronger entropy bonus, 3 epochs with entropy 0.03, and one cheap dilated residual conv for context.

## Trial it ended with
name: 2 epochs + entropy 0.03
hypothesis: Same as r2c1 (2 PPO epochs, about 231k steps) but ent_coef rises to 0.03. It tests the same anti-collapse fix at an epoch count between the stable 3-epoch r1c2 and the more sample-rich 1-epoch run. Compared with the 1-epoch candidate, it shows which epoch count is best once collapse is controlled. Refuted if a seed collapses to near 0, or if the mean is not above 0.89.
